instruction.text: Atifa spent 3/8 of her day studying. Then she had a nap for 2/4 of her day. What fraction of the day does she have left for other things?

atoms.a: Write the smallest common denominator of the two fractions.
Fill in the numerator of the equivalent fraction and then subtract the fraction.
atoms.b: She has <mat><gap>4</gap>/8 − 3/8 =<gap>1</gap>/8</mat> of her day left.

instruction.text: Lily is baking cupcakes. The recipe needs 3/7 kilograms of sugar and 11/49 kilograms of flour. How many total kilograms are required?

atoms.a: Write the smallest common denominator of the two fractions.
Fill in the numerator of the equivalent fraction and then add the fractions.
atoms.b: The recipe needs <mat><gap>21</gap>/49 + 11/49</mat> = <mat><gap>32</gap>/49</mat> kilograms in total.

instruction.text: Ali’s new garden is 2 2/3 of an acre. He wants to use 14/15 of an acre to plant vegetables. How much space does Ali have left over?

atoms.a: Convert the mixed number into an improper fraction.
Write the smallest common denominator of the two fractions.
Fill in the numerator of the equivalent fraction and then subtract the fraction.
Ali wants to plant 23/15 of an acre of flowers. Does he have enough space left over?
atoms.b: He ((++does doesn’t)) have enough space left over.

instruction.text: Layla is trying to finish reading her book by the end of the week. On Friday she had read 5/7 of the book. On Saturday she read 4/35. What fraction of the book does she have to read on Sunday in order to achieve her goal?

atoms.a: Write the smallest common denominator of the two fractions.
Fill in the numerator of the equivalent fraction and then add the fractions to find out how much of the book she has read already.

atoms.b: She still has to read <mat>35/35</mat> − <mat>29/35</mat> = <mat><gap>6</gap>/35</mat> of the book to finish in time.

instruction.text: Rajesh and his friends ordered 3 pizzas for a party. They ate 2/8 of the first pizza, 1/2 of the second, and 3/4 of the third. How much pizza did they eat in total?

atoms.a: Convert the fractions so they have the same denominator.

After a while, the group gets hungry again and eats 20/64 of one of the remaining pizzas. How much pizza did they eat in total?

12/8 + 20/64
atoms.b: They ate <mat><gap>96</gap>/64</mat> + <mat>20/64</mat> = <mat><gap>116</gap>/64</mat> of the pizzas in total.
